tasks.title: [r2-retry-status] isRetryableR2Status: which R2 reply statuses are worth retrying
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/r2-retry-status.ts` exporting `isRetryableR2Status(status: number): boolean`.

Behavior: given the HTTP status code of a reply from R2, answer true when the request is worth retrying and false when it is not. Worth retrying: 429 (too many requests) and every server error status from 500 through 599. Not worth retrying: everything else, including success, redirect and other client error statuses, and anything above 599.

Examples:
- 429 gives true
- 500 gives true
- 502 gives true
- 503 gives true
- 504 gives true
- 550 gives true
- 599 gives true
- 510 gives true
- 520 gives true
- 530 gives true
- 540 gives true
- 560 gives true
- 570 gives true
- 580 gives true
- 590 gives true
- 428 gives false
- 430 gives false
- 499 gives false
- 465 gives false
- 438 gives false
- 446 gives false
- 454 gives false
- 462 gives false
- 470 gives false
- 478 gives false
- 486 gives false
- 494 gives false
- 600 gives false
- 700 gives false
- 200 gives false
- 204 gives false
- 100 gives false
- 301 gives false
- 400 gives false
- 403 gives false
- 404 gives false
- 0 gives false

Context (Builder pre-file, refile of #486, behavior only): Peace's task (source: peace). The ten-minute chain stopped on R2_PUT_500 (run 39451888891) and R2_GET_500 (run 39467160610) because R2ObjectClient.request never retries; this is the status check the future retry will use. This issue states only the wanted behavior and example cases; PeaceAI has to work out the implementation itself. Production safety: one new function in a new module plus one new test file under src/ only. Nothing imports it yet, so the running scanner, the scan and the ten-minute chain are unchanged. Wiring it in is a separate task (see batch-v4/scanner/DIAGNOSIS.md).

tasks.title: [r2-retry-delay] r2RetryDelayMs: bounded backoff for an R2 retry attempt
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/r2-retry-delay.ts` exporting `r2RetryDelayMs(attempt: number, baseMs: number): number`.

Behavior: how many milliseconds to wait before retry number `attempt` (counting from 0), given a base wait of `baseMs`. Attempt 0 waits exactly the base. Each later attempt waits longer than the one before, following the pattern in the examples. The wait is never more than 30000 ms, whatever the attempt or base. A base of 0 always gives 0.

Examples (attempt, baseMs gives wait):
- 0, 1000 gives 1000
- 1, 1000 gives 4000
- 2, 1000 gives 9000
- 3, 1000 gives 16000
- 4, 1000 gives 25000
- 5, 1000 gives 30000
- 10, 1000 gives 30000
- 100, 1000 gives 30000
- 0, 500 gives 500
- 1, 500 gives 2000
- 2, 250 gives 2250
- 0, 0 gives 0
- 7, 0 gives 0
- 0, 40000 gives 30000

Context (Builder pre-file, refile of #487, behavior only): Peace's task (source: peace). The future R2 retry needs a wait that grows per attempt and never exceeds 30 seconds, so one retry cannot stall a scan. This issue states only the wanted behavior and example cases; PeaceAI has to work out the implementation itself. Production safety: one new function in a new module plus one new test file under src/ only. Nothing imports it yet, so the running scanner, the scan and the ten-minute chain are unchanged. Wiring it in is a separate task (see batch-v4/scanner/DIAGNOSIS.md).

tasks.title: [host-failure-line] hostFailureLine: host failure line that keeps the error cause code
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/host-failure-line.ts` exporting `hostFailureLine(message: string, causeCode: string): string`.

Behavior: build the one-line failure report the scheduler host prints. The line always starts with the marker MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED, then a colon, then the message exactly as given. When a cause code is given, the line ends with a colon, the word cause, an equals sign and the cause code. When the cause code is empty, nothing is added after the message. The message and cause code are copied as they are, with no trimming or escaping.

Examples (message, causeCode gives line):
- "fetch failed", "ECONNRESET" gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED:fetch failed:cause=ECONNRESET"
- "fetch failed", "" gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED:fetch failed"
- "R2_GET_500", "" gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED:R2_GET_500"
- "", "UND_ERR_SOCKET" gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED::cause=UND_ERR_SOCKET"
- "", "" gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED:"
- "R2_PUT_500", "ETIMEDOUT" gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED:R2_PUT_500:cause=ETIMEDOUT"
- " fetch failed ", "ECONNRESET" gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED: fetch failed :cause=ECONNRESET"
- "R2_GET_500", " err 42 " gives "MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED:R2_GET_500:cause= err 42 "

Context (Builder pre-file, refile of #488, behavior only): Peace's task (source: peace). Every scheduled scan since 2026-10-14 ends with only MARKETS_SCHEDULER_HOST_FAILED:fetch failed because src/host.ts drops the error cause; this is the line the host will print once wired, with the cause code (never a URL) appended when there is one. This issue states only the wanted behavior and example cases; PeaceAI has to work out the implementation itself. Production safety: one new function in a new module plus one new test file under src/ only. Nothing imports it yet, so the running scanner, the scan and the ten-minute chain are unchanged. Wiring it in is a separate task (see batch-v4/scanner/DIAGNOSIS.md).
